title: Physically Motivated Ansatz for Open Fermionic Systems on Quantum Computer
authors: Yi Liu, Xiaopeng Li, Zhen Liu, Zhenyu Li
abstract: Determining non-equilibrium steady states (NESS) of open fermionic systems is a fundamental problem akin to finding ground states of closed systems. To address this, variational quantum algorithms can be used to solve the Lindblad master equation, much like the Schrödinger equation, yet ansatz design for NESS remains challenging. Existing approaches rely mostly on hardware-efficient ansätze (HEA), which suffer from the barren plateau problem. Here, we introduce a physically motivated ansatz named NE-UCC. Numerical simulations demonstrate that NE-UCC reliably converges to the steady state even in strongly correlated regimes far from equilibrium, reducing the infidelity by up to ten orders of magnitude compared to HEA. Furthermore, NE-UCC facilitates the exploration of excited eigenmodes with specific symmetries.
summary: This paper tackles the challenging task of finding Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) for open fermionic systems using quantum computers. The authors introduce NE-UCC, a novel, physically motivated ansatz derived from Unitary Coupled Cluster theory adapted for Liouvillian dynamics. This method significantly outperforms existing variational approaches by maintaining high accuracy even in strongly correlated and far-from-equilibrium regimes.
main_problem: The core problem is determining Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) for open fermionic systems, which requires solving the Lindblad master equation.
main_result: The proposed NE-UCC ansatz reliably converges to the steady state with significantly reduced infidelity (up to ten orders of magnitude improvement) compared to standard Hardware-Efficient Ansätze (HEA).
method: The authors employ Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQA), specifically introducing a physically motivated ansatz called NE-UCC, which extends Unitary Coupled Cluster theory to incorporate weak Liouvillian symmetry.
model_or_system: The study models open fermionic systems governed by the Lindblad master equation. Specific examples include an XXZ boundary-driven transport model and a three-site quantum heat engine.
key_observables: Infidelity ($1 - |\langleho|ho_{ED}angle|^2$), Magnetization ($\langle M_j angle$), Particle Current ($\langle J_\alpha angle$), and the Liouvillian gap.
important_parameters: Strongly correlated regimes, far from equilibrium, and specific symmetry constraints derived from the superfermion formalism.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that standard UCC compilation strategies can be successfully applied to NE-UCC due to the adopted superfermion formalism mapping.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) compares NESS infidelity for the XXZ model across different ansatzes (dVQE, etc.). Figure 3 shows accurate current vs. bias potential curves for the heat engine using NE-UCC versus failures of dVQE. Figure 4 compares Liouvillian gap precision.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of NESS determination via VQA, proposes and details the NE-UCC ansatz based on weak symmetry constraints, validates its performance against HEA using benchmark models (XXZ chain, heat engine), and discusses extensions like ADAPT-NE-UCC.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses computational bottlenecks in simulating open quantum systems by providing a physically informed variational ansatz that overcomes the barren plateau problem inherent to general VQAs.
